change_interpretations.engineering_summary: A new requirement mandates that the controller records timestamped mode changes along with the software build identifier. This is a functional addition to the logging scope. Verification must ensure that mode transitions (e.g., Comfort to Sport) are captured with both a timestamp and the build ID. The removed requirement VCU-LOG-05 had identical text, so this is effectively a re-identification of an existing requirement rather than a behavioral change. Existing tests that verify this behavior (like TV-006) remain valid but need their links updated to the new requirement ID.

The requirement for recording timestamped mode changes and software build identifiers has been removed from the specification. However, since VCU-LOG-15 was added with identical text, this removal is likely part of a re-identification or consolidation. Tests linked to this requirement (like TV-006) should be re-linked to VCU-LOG-15 rather than retired, as the behavior is still required under the new ID.

assessments.reason: The test verifies driver torque response timing (VCU-DR-01), which is not part of the specification change. The change only adds a logging requirement (VCU-LOG-15) and removes its predecessor (VCU-LOG-05), neither of which affects torque timing behavior.
evidence: Test verifies torque response time (94 ms) against VCU-DR-01, which is unchanged.
No relation to the added logging requirement VCU-LOG-15.
assessments.recommended_action: No action required for this change.

assessments.reason: The test exercises brake/pedal arbitration and torque response, governed by unchanged requirements VCU-BRK-03 and VCU-DR-01. It does not verify the new logging requirement VCU-LOG-15.
evidence: Test verifies brake override priority (VCU-BRK-03) and torque response (VCU-DR-01), both unchanged.
No logging of mode changes or build IDs is part of the procedure.
assessments.recommended_action: No action required for this change.
